question: Which of the following ruler was Brahmins who gave up their traditional professions and established kingdom in Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurjara-Pratihara Harichandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harichandra was a Brahmin who abandoned his traditional priestly profession and founded a Pratihara (Gurjara-Pratihara) kingdom in Rajasthan around Mandavyapura (Mandore, near Jodhpur).

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas (गुर्जर-प्रतिहार) later rose to become one of the most powerful dynasties of northern India during the early medieval period.

• The Mandore branch traced its origin to this Brahmin ruler Harichandra and his wife Bhadra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The imperial Gurjara-Pratiharas of Kannauj were pivotal in the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj against the Palas and the Rashtrakutas.

• King Mihir Bhoja (Bhoja I) was the greatest ruler of the imperial Pratihara line.

• The Pratiharas are credited with checking Arab incursions into India for a long time.

NOTE

• Dantidurga (Option 1): Founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, who overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami in the 8th century.

• Nagabhata (Option 3): Name of Pratihara kings (Nagabhata I and II); Nagabhata I resisted Arab invasions, but he was not the Brahmin founder described here.

• Dharmapala Deva (Option 4): A powerful ruler of the Pala dynasty of Bengal and Bihar, founder of the Vikramashila and Somapura viharas.

question: Which Mughal ruler made Gakkhar chief Kamal Khan, a Mansabdar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mughal emperor Akbar conferred a Mansab (rank) on the Gakkhar chief Kamal Khan, making him a Mansabdar (मनसबदार).

• The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar to organise the nobility, military and civil administration on the basis of numerical ranks (mansabs).

• Each mansabdar held two ranks — Zat (personal status/pay) and Sawar (number of cavalry to maintain).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Gakkhars were a warlike tribe of the Pothohar/Punjab region who were loyal allies of the Mughals against Sher Shah Suri's successors.

• Mansabs ranged in theory from 10 up to 10,000 (higher ranks reserved for princes of royal blood).

• Mansabdars were paid either in cash (naqdi) or through revenue assignments called Jagirs.

NOTE

• Babur (Option 1): Founder of the Mughal Empire who won the First Battle of Panipat (1526); he did not establish the mansabdari system.

• Shah Jahan (Option 3): Mughal emperor famous for building the Taj Mahal; ruled long after the Gakkhar chief was enrolled.

• Aurangzeb (Option 4): The last of the great Mughals, known for his Deccan campaigns and expansion of the empire to its greatest extent.

question: _____ has secured the top position in India in the Times Higher Education (THE) Asia Rankings 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Institute of Science.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru secured the top position among Indian institutions in the Times Higher Education (THE) Asia University Rankings 2025.

• IISc has consistently been the highest-ranked Indian institution (भारतीय विज्ञान संस्थान) in the THE Asia rankings.

• The THE rankings assess universities on teaching, research environment, research quality, international outlook and industry engagement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• IISc was established in 1909 with the support of Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata and the Maharaja of Mysore.

• It is a public, deemed-to-be university with an Institute of Eminence tag.

• In the THE Asia 2025 list several IITs also featured, but IISc remained India's best.

NOTE

• IIT Lucknow (Option 2): There is no IIT at Lucknow; it is a distractor (IIM Lucknow exists, not IIT).

• IIT Bombay (Option 3): A top IIT and consistently high in NIRF and QS rankings, but not India's number one in THE Asia 2025.

• IIT Kanpur (Option 4): A premier IIT known for engineering and computer science, but ranked below IISc in THE Asia 2025.

question: The term 'Raider' is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabaddi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The term 'Raider' is associated with the sport of Kabaddi (कबड्डी).

• In Kabaddi, the raider is the player who crosses into the opponents' half chanting 'kabaddi' to tag defenders and return safely to earn points.

• The defending players who try to stop the raider are called antis/stoppers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kabaddi is the state game of many Indian states and India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and Asian Games.

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) popularised professional kabaddi in India from 2014.

• Common terms include Raid, Bonus Line, Baulk Line, and Do-or-Die Raid.

NOTE

• Badminton (Option 2): Uses terms like smash, drop, service and shuttlecock — not raider.

• Lawn tennis (Option 3): Uses terms such as ace, deuce, volley and love.

• Cricket (Option 4): Uses terms like over, wicket, googly and boundary.

question: In 2025, Mumbai Marathon was held in which month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is January.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tata Mumbai Marathon 2025 (its 20th edition) was held in the month of January (जनवरी), on 19 January 2025.

• The Mumbai Marathon is India's largest and most prestigious mass-participation running event.

• It is traditionally held in January every year in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The event is organised by Procam International and is a World Athletics Elite Label road race.

• It features categories such as the Full Marathon (42.195 km), Half Marathon, Dream Run and Senior Citizens' Run.

• The marathon began in 2004 and is a major charity fund-raising platform.

NOTE

• March (Option 2): Not the month of the Mumbai Marathon.

• July (Option 3): Falls in the monsoon season, unsuitable for the marathon in Mumbai.

• February (Option 4): The event is held in January, not February.

question: Which of the following books has NOT been written by Amitav Ghosh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Ground Beneath Her Feet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ground Beneath Her Feet (1999) was written by Salman Rushdie, NOT by Amitav Ghosh (अमिताव घोष).

• Amitav Ghosh is a celebrated Indian author who wrote The Glass Palace, The Hungry Tide and The Imam and the Indian.

• Since the question asks which book Ghosh did NOT write, the odd one out is Rushdie's novel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amitav Ghosh won the Jnanpith Award (2018), the first English-language writer to receive it.

• His famous Ibis Trilogy comprises *Sea of Poppies*, *River of Smoke* and *Flood of Fire*.

• *The Ground Beneath Her Feet* by Rushdie reimagines the Orpheus myth in a rock-music setting.

NOTE

• The Glass Palace (Option 1): A historical novel by Amitav Ghosh set in Burma, Bengal and Malaya.

• The Imam and the Indian (Option 2): A collection of essays by Amitav Ghosh.

• The Hungry Tide (Option 3): A novel by Amitav Ghosh set in the Sundarbans.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Guerrillas' published in 1975?
solution_text:
The correct answer is V. S. Naipaul.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The novel 'Guerrillas' (1975) was written by V. S. Naipaul (वी. एस. नायपॉल).

• The book is set on a fictional Caribbean island and explores themes of revolution, race and disillusionment.

• V. S. Naipaul was a Trinidad-born British writer of Indian descent.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Naipaul won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001 and the Booker Prize in 1971 for *In a Free State*.

• His notable works include *A House for Mr Biswas*, *A Bend in the River* and *India: A Wounded Civilization*.

• He was knighted in 1990.

NOTE

• Novoneel Chakraborty (Option 1): A contemporary Indian author of romance and thriller novels like the *Stranger Trilogy*.

• Bapsi Sidhwa (Option 3): A Pakistani-American novelist known for *Ice-Candy-Man (Cracking India)*.

• Mohsin Hamid (Option 4): A Pakistani author famous for *The Reluctant Fundamentalist*.

question: Which of the following novel has been authored by Anita Desai?
option_2: I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale
option_3: Where Shall We Go This Summer
solution_text:
The correct answer is Where Shall We Go This Summer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The novel 'Where Shall We Go This Summer?' (1975) was authored by Anita Desai (अनीता देसाई).

• The novel explores the inner emotional world and psychological conflict of its female protagonist Sita.

• Anita Desai is noted for her deep exploration of the psyche of her characters.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Anita Desai has been shortlisted for the Booker Prize three times (for *Clear Light of Day*, *In Custody* and *Fasting, Feasting*).

• Her novel In Custody was made into a Merchant Ivory film.

• Her daughter Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize in 2006 for *The Inheritance of Loss*.

NOTE

• Book of Humour (Option 1): Not an Anita Desai novel; a generic/distractor title.

• I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale (Option 2): A novel by Khushwant Singh.

• The Struggle for India's Soul (Option 4): Not authored by Anita Desai; a distractor title.

question: 'Shad Suk Mynsiem' festival is celebrated in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Shad Suk Mynsiem' is a famous festival celebrated by the Khasi people of Meghalaya (मेघालय).

• The name translates to the 'Dance of the Joyful Heart' and is a thanksgiving dance festival held in spring.

• Unmarried young men and women perform the traditional dance in colourful attire.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Meghalaya's capital is Shillong, and its major tribes are the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo.

• Other Meghalaya festivals include Wangala (Garo), Nongkrem Dance and Behdienkhlam (Jaintia).

• Meghalaya means the 'abode of clouds'.

NOTE

• Ladakh (Option 1): Known for festivals like Hemis and Losar, not Shad Suk Mynsiem.

• Assam (Option 3): Famous for the Bihu festival.

• Gujarat (Option 4): Known for Navratri (Garba) and the Rann Utsav.

question: The red sandstone tower of Qutb Minar has _____ meters diameter at its base
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.32.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Qutb Minar has a base diameter of about 14.32 metres, tapering to roughly 2.75 metres at the top.

• It is a red sandstone (लाल बलुआ पत्थर) and marble tower and the tallest brick minaret in the world, about 72.5 metres high.

• It is located at the Qutb Complex in Mehrauli, Delhi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Its construction was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (founder of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty) around 1199 and completed by Iltutmish.

• It has five storeys, each marked by a projecting balcony.

• Nearby stands the famous Iron Pillar of Delhi, noted for its rust resistance.

NOTE

• 16.32 (Option 2): An overstated value; the base diameter is 14.32 m.

• 10.32 (Option 3): Too small to be the base diameter of the Qutb Minar.

• 12.32 (Option 4): Incorrect value for the base diameter.

question: _____ is performed in front of an image of the Goddess Mariamman in Tamil Nadu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karakattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Karakattam is a traditional folk dance of Tamil Nadu performed in praise of Mariamman (देवी मरियम्मन), the goddess of rain.

• Dancers balance a decorated pot (karagam) filled with uncooked rice on their heads while dancing.

• It is performed to invoke blessings for rain and a good harvest.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Karakattam is set to the music of instruments like the naiyandi melam.

• It has two forms — Aatta Karagam (for entertainment) and Sakthi Karagam (devotional).

• Mariamman is a prominent mother-goddess of rural South India.

NOTE

• Villu Pattu (Option 2): A traditional Tamil ballad/musical storytelling art form using a bow-shaped instrument.

• Sevai Attam (Option 3): A distractor; not the dance performed before Mariamman.

• Kolattam (Option 4): A stick dance of Tamil Nadu performed by women, similar to dandiya, but not specifically before Mariamman.

question: The Mars Orbiter Mission of India was launched in _____
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2013.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), also called Mangalyaan (मंगल ऑर्बिटर मिशन), was launched on 5 November 2013 from Sriharikota.

• It successfully entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.

• India became the first country to reach Mars orbit in its very first attempt.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• MOM was launched by the PSLV-C25 rocket by ISRO.

• It made India the first Asian nation and the fourth space agency to reach Mars.

• The mission was highly cost-effective, costing about ₹450 crore.

NOTE

• 2006 (Option 1): Not related to the Mars mission; too early.

• 2009 (Option 2): The year Chandrayaan-1 confirmed water on the Moon, not the Mars launch year.

• 2019 (Option 4): The year of Chandrayaan-2 (Moon mission), not MOM.

question: Which of the following gas is used in homes for cooking?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liquefied petroleum gas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) (द्रवीकृत पेट्रोलियम गैस) is used in homes for cooking.

• LPG is mainly a mixture of butane and propane hydrocarbons.

• A strong-smelling odorant, ethyl mercaptan, is added to LPG so that leaks can be detected easily.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• LPG is stored under pressure in liquid form in cylinders.

• It is a clean fuel that burns to give a high amount of heat with little smoke.

• The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides LPG connections to households.

NOTE

• Argon gas (Option 1): An inert gas used in electric bulbs and welding, not for cooking.

• Nitrogen gas (Option 2): An inert gas used in packaging and to make ammonia/fertilizers.

• Oxygen gas (Option 4): Supports combustion and is used medically, but is not the cooking fuel itself.

question: The forces of attraction between the particles are maximum in _____ and minimum in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is solids, gases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The force of attraction (आकर्षण बल) between particles is maximum in solids and minimum in gases.

• In solids, particles are closely packed with strong intermolecular forces, giving a fixed shape and volume.

• In gases, particles are far apart with very weak forces, so gases have neither a fixed shape nor volume.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The order of intermolecular force of attraction is solids > liquids > gases.

• Liquids have moderate forces — fixed volume but no fixed shape.

• The kinetic energy of particles is highest in gases and lowest in solids.

NOTE

• gases, liquid (Option 2): Incorrect; gases have the weakest, not the strongest forces.

• solids, liquid (Option 3): Solids have maximum force, but the minimum is in gases, not liquids.

• gases, solids (Option 4): This reverses the correct order.

question: In January 2025, which became the first indigenous robotic system of India to performed two cardiac surgeries through telesurgery over a distance of 286 km?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SSI Mantra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the SSI Mantra (एस.एस.आई. मंत्रा) became the first indigenous (make-in-India) surgical robotic system to perform two cardiac telesurgeries over a distance of about 286 km.

• It was developed by SS Innovations International.

• This made it the world's first robotic cardiac telesurgery using an Indian-made system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Telesurgery allows a surgeon to operate on a patient located at a remote distance using a robotic system.

• The SSI Mantra is a cost-effective indigenous alternative to imported surgical robots.

• Such systems can help extend expert surgical care to rural and remote areas.

NOTE

• Da Vinci (Option 1): A widely used surgical robotic system made by the US company Intuitive Surgical — not indigenous to India.

• Mitra (Option 2): An Indian humanoid social robot, not a surgical robot.

• Robonaut (Option 4): A humanoid robot developed by NASA for space tasks.

question: The estimates of revenue receipts take into account the effects of tax proposals made in the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Finance bill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The estimates of revenue receipts take into account the effects of tax proposals made in the Finance Bill (वित्त विधेयक).

• The Finance Bill contains the government's proposals for the imposition, abolition, alteration or regulation of taxes for the coming year.

• It is presented in the Lok Sabha along with the Union Budget every year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A Finance Bill is a type of Money Bill under Article 110 of the Constitution.

• The Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes to a Money Bill; the Lok Sabha may accept or reject them.

• The Finance Bill must be passed within 75 days of its introduction.

NOTE

• Appropriation bill (Option 2): Authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet expenditure — it does not deal with tax proposals.

• Constitution amendment bill (Option 3): Used to amend provisions of the Constitution under Article 368.

• Demand for grant bill (Option 4): Relates to the estimates of expenditure, presented as demands for grants voted by the Lok Sabha.

question: The Battle of Buxar took place in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1764.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Buxar (बक्सर का युद्ध) was fought in 1764 between the British East India Company and a combined army.

• The combined forces were led by Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and Shah Alam II (Mughal Emperor).

• The British, led by Hector Munro, decisively defeated the allied Indian forces.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The victory led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), giving the Company the Diwani rights (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

• This battle firmly established British political and financial supremacy in eastern India.

• Robert Clive negotiated the Treaty of Allahabad with Shah Alam II.

NOTE

• 1757 (Option 1): The year of the Battle of Plassey, won by Robert Clive against Siraj-ud-Daula.

• 1773 (Option 3): The year of the Regulating Act, not the Battle of Buxar.

• 1785 (Option 4): No battle of this significance; a distractor.

question: After the indigo revolution in Bengal, where did the planters shift their operations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the Indigo Revolt (Nil Bidroha) in Bengal (1859-60), the indigo planters shifted their operations to Bihar (बिहार).

• The Bengal revolt made indigo cultivation there unviable, so plantations moved to Bihar's Champaran region.

• This later led to the exploitation of Champaran peasants under the tinkathia system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The exploitation in Bihar sparked the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Mahatma Gandhi's first satyagraha in India.

• The Bengal Indigo Revolt was led by peasants like Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas.

• The play 'Nil Darpan' by Dinabandhu Mitra depicted the sufferings of indigo cultivators.

NOTE

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Associated with the Deccan Riots (1875) over moneylenders, not indigo relocation.

• Karnataka (Option 3): Not connected with the shift of indigo planters.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Not the destination of the relocated indigo planters.

question: Merchandise Exports from India Scheme was launched in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS) was launched in 2015 under the Foreign Trade Policy 2015-20.

• It aimed to promote the export of notified goods/merchandise by providing incentives in the form of Duty Credit Scrips.

• It merged and replaced five earlier export incentive schemes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• MEIS was administered by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

• It was later replaced by the RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) scheme from January 2021.

• The scrips could be used to pay customs duties and were transferable.

NOTE

• 1998 (Option 1): Not the launch year of MEIS.

• 2002 (Option 2): A distractor; MEIS did not exist then.

• 2019 (Option 3): MEIS was already running; RoDTEP was announced around this time as a replacement.

question: Which of the following was NOT the goal of five year plans in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dependency on foreign aid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dependency on foreign aid (विदेशी सहायता पर निर्भरता) was NOT a goal of India's Five Year Plans; rather, self-reliance (Atmanirbharta) was a key objective.

• The four main goals of the Five Year Plans were Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity.

• The aim was to reduce dependence on imports and foreign aid, not increase it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's Five Year Plans were formulated by the Planning Commission (established 1950), later replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

• Growth meant an increase in the country's capacity to produce goods and services.

• Equity ensured that the benefits of growth reached all sections of society.

NOTE

• Growth (Option 1): A genuine goal — increasing GDP and productive capacity.

• Modernisation (Option 3): A genuine goal — adopting new technology and progressive social outlook.

• Equity (Option 4): A genuine goal — ensuring fair distribution and reducing inequality.

question: Which of the following five year plan in India was thorough failure in reaching targets due to unforeseen events like Chinese aggression (1962)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Third.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) (तीसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना) was a near-total failure in achieving its targets.

• It was derailed by unforeseen events like the Chinese aggression of 1962, the Indo-Pak war of 1965 and severe droughts/famine.

• These crises diverted resources to defence and disrupted economic planning.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Third Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model with emphasis on making the economy self-reliant.

• Its failure led to the period of 'Plan Holidays' (1966-69) with three annual plans.

• The wars caused inflation and forced a devaluation of the rupee in 1966.

NOTE

• First (Option 1): The First Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and was largely successful, focusing on agriculture.

• Second (Option 2): The Second Plan (1956-61) focused on heavy industry under the Mahalanobis model.

• Fifth (Option 4): The Fifth Plan (1974-78) focused on 'Garibi Hatao' (poverty removal) and self-reliance.

question: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act-2003 requires the reduction in revenue deficit by _____ of GDP every year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.5%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 (वित्तीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम) required the reduction of the revenue deficit by 0.5% of GDP every year.

• It also mandated reducing the fiscal deficit by 0.3% of GDP annually.

• The Act aimed to bring fiscal discipline and reduce government borrowing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FRBM Act's original targets were to eliminate the revenue deficit and cut the fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP.

• The N. K. Singh Committee reviewed the FRBM framework and recommended a debt-to-GDP target of 60%.

• The Act provides for an escape clause allowing deviation from targets in exceptional circumstances.

NOTE

• 2.5% (Option 2): Not the mandated annual reduction figure for revenue deficit.

• 4% (Option 3): An incorrect value; a distractor.

• 6% (Option 4): Incorrect; the annual revenue deficit reduction was 0.5%.

question: How many carbon molecules does pyruvate has?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pyruvate (pyruvic acid) is a three-carbon (3C) molecule (तीन कार्बन अणु).

• It is the end product of glycolysis, in which one six-carbon glucose molecule is split into two three-carbon pyruvate molecules.

• Its chemical formula is C3H4O3.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell.

• In aerobic respiration, pyruvate enters the mitochondria and is converted to acetyl-CoA (2 carbon), releasing CO2.

• In the absence of oxygen, pyruvate is converted to lactic acid or ethanol (fermentation).

NOTE

• 4 (Option 2): Not the number of carbons in pyruvate; oxaloacetate is a 4-carbon molecule.

• 5 (Option 3): Alpha-ketoglutarate is a 5-carbon molecule, not pyruvate.

• 6 (Option 4): Glucose and citrate have 6 carbons, not pyruvate.

question: 'Daimabad', a Harappan site, is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Daimabad is a Harappan (Indus Valley Civilization) site located in Maharashtra (महाराष्ट्र), on the banks of the Pravara River in Ahmednagar district.

• It is the southernmost site of the Harappan civilization.

• Daimabad is famous for its bronze artefacts, including the bronze chariot, buffalo, elephant and rhinoceros.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The famous Bronze Chariot of Daimabad is a notable example of Harappan metallurgy.

• The site was discovered in 1958.

• It shows evidence of Late Harappan and later cultural phases in the Deccan.

NOTE

• Haryana (Option 1): Home to Harappan sites like Rakhigarhi, Banawali and Mitathal.

• Punjab (Option 2): Site of Ropar (Rupnagar), a Harappan settlement.

• Gujarat (Option 3): Contains sites like Lothal, Dholavira, Rangpur and Surkotada.

question: Who was the composer of the Allahabad pillar inscription of Samudragupta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harisena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti) of Samudragupta was composed by his court poet Harisena (हरिसेन).

• It is written in classical Sanskrit in the Champu style (mix of prose and verse).

• The inscription glorifies the military conquests and achievements of Samudragupta.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The inscription is engraved on the same Ashokan pillar that bears the edicts of Emperor Ashoka.

• Samudragupta is often called the 'Napoleon of India' (a term coined by historian V. A. Smith) for his conquests.

• Harisena held high offices such as Sandhivigrahika (minister of war and peace).

NOTE

• Simuka (Option 1): The founder of the Satavahana dynasty.

• Kalidasa (Option 2): A great Sanskrit poet and dramatist (author of *Abhijnanashakuntalam*), associated with Chandragupta II's court, not this inscription.

• Simhavishnu (Option 4): An early ruler of the Pallava dynasty of South India.
